name: Demande d'asile / Protection internationale

requirements.blocker_text: This can only be claimed while on French territory or at a border post.

This requires meeting one of two categories assessed by OFPRA: statut de réfugié (refugee status, Geneva Convention grounds) or protection subsidiaire (subsidiary protection, real risk of serious harm).

evidence_required.document: Evidence supporting the persecution or serious-harm claim

outcome.duration_length: refugee status: 10 years, renewable; subsidiary protection: 4 years, renewable subject to reassessment

sources.title: OFPRA — Office Français de Protection des Réfugiés et Apatrides

notes: No application fee, consistent with every other country's asylum route in this dataset. Refugee status carries a genuinely long 10-year card duration — longer than any other country's refugee-status duration encoded in this dataset (UK 5 years to ILR-eligibility, Germany 3 years, Netherlands 5 years, Portugal 5 years, Spain 5 years), worth flagging as a real, confirmed outlier. Two-tier appeal system (CNDA — Cour Nationale du Droit d'Asile) exists for rejected OFPRA claims — not modeled as a separate schema element but genuinely relevant to realistic processing-time expectations, since first-instance-plus-appeal timelines commonly run well beyond any single statutory figure, a pattern flagged similarly across Portugal's AIMA backlog notes and Italy's OFPRA-equivalent context in the France research itself.
